title: Cycle evaluation descends to homology
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], T and J integer cochain complexes of O_X-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and n an integer. With the projection and cycle-evaluation predicate defined in [new-b2-homology-evaluation-definitions], there exists e:H^n(Hom(T,J)) -> Hom(H^(-n)(T),H^0(J)) satisfying the cycle formula, with no concentration, K-injectivity or finite-free hypothesis.

source.place: sites-cohomology.tex, section-hom-complexes; cohomology.tex, section-internal-hom (08DH), complex evaluation; duality.tex, lemma-regular-ideal-ext (0BQY), zero-differential Hom calculation.

proof.text: Apply homComplex_projections_exists to the chosen Hom-complex. Its differential equation is the only property of the projections used. In the private algebraic helpers the complex and projections are abstract parameters, preventing reduction of the large chosen bifunctor.

Restrict the degree-n projection at (-n,0) to cycles of both complexes. Apply the Hom differential equation at (-n,1), then the source-cycle equation, to show that postcomposition with d_J is zero. Uncurry by the tensor-Hom adjunction, lift into J-cycles by HomologicalComplex.liftCycles, and curry back. Naturality of tensorHomEquiv gives its equation after the inclusion into J^0.

Postcompose the cycle lift with J.homologyπ. For a Hom boundary the differential formula at degree n-1 evaluated on a T-cycle gives the lift through J.toCycles (-1) 0. For a T boundary the cocycle equation at source degree -n-1 gives the same lift multiplied by n.negOnePow. Cancel the mono obtained by applying internal Hom to J.iCycles. In both cases J.toCycles_comp_homologyπ makes the result zero. The sign is its own inverse by Int.units_mul_self.

Descend first through P.homologyIsCokernel. The resulting map still kills T boundaries by cancellation of the epi P.homologyπ. For the T quotient, uncurry the map and apply CokernelCofork.mapIsColimit to tensorRight, which preserves colimits because it is a left adjoint. Its cokernel descent, curried back, is e. The two cofork factorization identities give (P.homologyπ >> e) >> homObjMap T.homologyπ identity equal to the cycle pairing.

Evaluate the preceding morphism identity at an open U and two cycle representatives. Evaluate the cycle lift identity as well. Evaluation preserves monos, so the value of the lift in J-cycles equals any supplied b with the same inclusion into J^0. Postcomposition with J.homologyπ gives exactly IsHomologyEvaluation. No sectionwise surjectivity of homologyπ or extra hypotheses are used.

mathlib_searches.results: Eight additive-group Hom-complex cohomology declarations, including CochainComplex.HomComplex.homologyAddEquiv; none constructs this sheaf-valued evaluation or proves its local perfection.
Twelve declarations, including homologyIsCokernel and instEpiHomologyπ. Useful universal properties, but no bilinear internal-Hom evaluation theorem.
One Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/Functor.lean match concerning evaluation of a diagram of complexes; no internal-Hom evaluation theorem.

from.place: Local zero-differential Koszul self-Ext calculation; homology evaluation subargument: Steps 1 and 2: descending the cycle pairing through homology cokernels.

lean.statement: theorem exists_homologyEvaluation_cycle (X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}) (T J : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ) (n : ℤ) : ∃ e : (homComplex (R := X.sheaf) T J).homology n ⟶ SheafOfModules.homObj (R := X.sheaf) (T.homology (-n)) (J.homology 0), IsHomologyEvaluation X T J n e
